note: [agent-bulk] SAME GEOMETRY AS evt53658 IN THIS SHARD, and here it is unambiguous. Vertex judged from a --vtx-span 60 re-capture (event_half_span_cm reads 400.0 but that is the clip: r95 is 412.3, so the event is wider than the number admits) plus ov-xz. In ov-xz the star (-133.3,108.4,1.3) sits EXACTLY on the bottom red bounding-box line, i.e. the z=0 TPC upstream face, at the end of segment 23000 -- a 466.8 cm pdg-13 track running from (-106,171,438) down to the star. In the +-60 cm close-in view there is NOTHING at the star except that one track terminating on it: no hadronic prong, no second object, no charge off-axis. The only convergence in the event is a three-way junction 119 cm up the track at (-129,130,119), where 23004 (58.2 cm pdg 13) and 23005 (82.9 cm pdg 13) branch off. A 467 cm track entering the upstream face with the vertex pinned at its entry point is a through-going / entering particle, not a contained neutrino interaction, so the vertex is not usable as a shower reference and the rubric's first test fires. This retroactively STRENGTHENS my evt53658 call: same face, same single-track-on-the-star signature, but there the track was only 72 cm and I left the alternative (a real interaction 1 cm inside the face) open at confidence likely. Two of ten events in this shard have the vertex within ~1.3 cm of z=0 -- that is worth the owner's attention as a pattern, not as two separate events. NO CLUSTERING JUDGEMENT is carried by this verdict. SEPARATE FLAG, not a recorded PID verdict (correction 6): neither in-scope object is an EM shower. 72009 (228.4 MeV, table length 84.4 cm) is two segments -- a 1.4 cm 3-point seed plus 23005, an 82.9 cm pdg-13 segment -- and in the 3-D view at az-055 the yellow member set is one straight, narrow, uniform-width line running parallel to and alongside the big muon, with no cone and no widening anywhere along it; 228.4 MeV over 84.4 cm is 2.7 MeV/cm, i.e. MIP-like, consistent with a track. 23004 (kine_charge 99.6, kine_best 162.0, reco pdg 13, 58.2 cm, conn 4) is the other branch of the same junction and is likewise a track. So both in-scope EM showers here are pieces of one muon-like track complex. NOT looked at: 71008, 28006, 29007, all under 1.6 MeV. No pi0: kine_div says no reco group, both in-scope showers have pio_id -1, and no pio-*.png slots were filled (pio slots None). Only 3 images looked at, which is the right number for a 7-segment event (correction 13). drag_check live: probe_radius_px 236, seg_u 58.03 -> 66.68, cloud_u 14.94 -> 21.93, cloud_redrew true, probe_degenerate false.
